To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

isoprenylflavonoids are formed through an enzymic Diels-Alder-type reaction between an isopenylphenol and a chalcone and that two independent pathways for isoprenoids exist in the Morus cell cultures.

the mulberry Diel-Alder type adducst were proved to be the products of the enzymatic Diels-Alter type reaction between an α, β-unsaturated carbonyl moiety of a chalcone and an isoprenoid moiety of an isopreynlphenol.
the mulberry Diel-Alder type adduction is an enzyme catalyzed reaction, and the isoprenylflavonoids are formed through the isoprenylation pathway of the glycolysis-pentose phosphate pathway junction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemistry and biosynthesis of mulberry flavonoids.
the biosynthesis of isoflavonoids, especially Diels-Alder adducts, in Morus albus cell cultures.
the biosynthesis and biological activities of isoprenoid flavonoids in Moraceae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mulberry Diels- Alder type adducts are biosynthesized by an enzyme-catalysed reaction of isoprenoid phenol and chalcone in Morus albo callus tissues, and the enzyme is a dienophilic flavone synthase.
the mulberry Diel-Alder type addducts are formed by the Diels-Alderase reaction between the isoprenyl group of isoprenoid phenol as the dienophiles and the double bond of chalcones as the dienes.
isoprenyl phenols are biosynthesized via the non-mevalonate pathway and the isoprenylflavonoids are synthesized via the mevalonate pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biosynthesis of mulberry Dielis-Alder type adducrs is a unique and interesting phenomenon.

the isoprenylflavonoid biosynthesis is controlled by the balance of two different metabolic pathways, the sterol and the prenylphenol biosynthetic pathway, which are regulated by the supply of mevalonic acid and the administration of compactin.
the Diels-Aldertype adducts are formed through a novel type of enzyme-catalyzed reaction between an isopenylphenol and a flavonoid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthetic pathway of isoprenoidflavonoids is not the same as that of isoprenoids in general.
the Diels-Alder type adducts are formed in Morus al ba cell cultures by an enzymatic process.
the Diels-Alderase is a novel type of enzyme which catalyzes a Diels-Alder-type reaction in the plant cell.
